svg.title: Qualify the Mortgage-Foreclosure Claim
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-mortgage-surplus-qualification; chapter number: 5; title: Qualify the Mortgage-Foreclosure Claim; subtitle: A sale-price gap does not establish available funds, claimant priority, or a complete filing.; caption: Eric Richardson of Money Making Juggernaut checks actual debt, trustee disbursements, and prior claims. Friscia & Associates describes service and authority checks for a New Jersey motion.; assumptions note: Richardson distinguishes county-held judicial funds from trustee-held nonjudicial funds. Friscia & Associates' motion requirements describe the New Jersey procedure discussed, not a universal filing packet.; note: Sternberg Law Group distinguishes a third-party winning bid from a bank-owned outcome. Richardson warns that an opening bid may not represent the amount actually owed.; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Did the sale produce a candidate after checking the final judgment or writ rather than only the opening bid?; pass next: G2; fail action: Retrieve the sale result and actual debt record. Do not treat a bank-owned outcome as proven surplus.; gate: G2; question: Does the holding office's disbursement breakdown establish that money remains after creditor payments?; pass next: G3; fail action: Request the trustee's disbursement history. Pause owner-recovery pursuit until remaining funds are established.; gate: G3; question: Has prior contact and existing claim activity been checked?; pass next: G4; fail action: Ask the claimant about prior recovery contact and submitted claims, and resolve the existing-claim status.; gate: G4; question: Are ownership, authority, relevant liens, and the applicable filing requirements established?; pass next: Proceed through the applicable court or trustee claim route.; fail action: Resolve missing authority or filing defects. For Friscia's New Jersey motion, check party service, estate authority when needed, and agreement between the proposed order and court amounts.

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Did the sale produce a candidate after checking the final judgment or writ rather than only the opening bid?; pass next: G2; fail action: Retrieve the sale result and actual debt record. Do not treat a bank-owned outcome as proven surplus.

gate: G2; question: Does the holding office's disbursement breakdown establish that money remains after creditor payments?; pass next: G3; fail action: Request the trustee's disbursement history. Pause owner-recovery pursuit until remaining funds are established.

gate: G3; question: Has prior contact and existing claim activity been checked?; pass next: G4; fail action: Ask the claimant about prior recovery contact and submitted claims, and resolve the existing-claim status.

gate: G4; question: Are ownership, authority, relevant liens, and the applicable filing requirements established?; pass next: Proceed through the applicable court or trustee claim route.; fail action: Resolve missing authority or filing defects. For Friscia's New Jersey motion, check party service, estate authority when needed, and agreement between the proposed order and court amounts.

text.title: Assumptions: Richardson distinguishes county-held judicial funds from trustee-held nonjudicial funds. Friscia & Associates' motion requirements describe the New Jersey procedure discussed, not a universal filing packet.
